c.tagline: City of pearls and biryani, where Nizami palaces meet the glass towers of HITEC City.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws are metered by law but drivers often quote a flat fare, so agree the price or insist on the meter before starting; app cabs (Uber/Ola) and Rapido bikes are usually cheaper and hassle-free.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified single emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 108 is the free ambulance service and 100 the police helpline.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing is common in the crowded Charminar/Laad Bazaar lanes and on buses; avoid poorly lit Old City backstreets late at night.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Hyderabad around the 1591 Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, and the bangle-lined Laad Bazaar; crowded and chaotic but unbeatable for monuments, pearl and bangle shopping, and legendary Old City biryani.

An upscale district of designer boutiques, fine-dining restaurants, rooftop bars, top hospitals, and the leafy Road No. 1 and Road No. 12; suits travelers who want comfort, shopping, and nightlife close together.

A posh residential-and-entertainment area home to film celebrities, the forested KBR National Park, trendy cafes, clubs, and the Jubilee Hills Check Post; good for upscale dining and stylish nightlife.

Hyderabad's modern IT corridor of glass office towers, malls like Inorbit and Sarath City, business hotels, breweries, and coworking spaces around Cyber Towers and the Financial District; the convenient base for tech and business travelers.
The colonial twin city with a cantonment feel, the landmark Clock Tower, Parade Ground, and the main railway junction; more local, calmer, and easier on the budget than central Hyderabad.

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Hyderabad Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; TSRTC city buses run from early morning to around 11:00 PM, with app cabs and autos filling late-night gaps.
transit.note: Hyderabad Metro Rail is one of India's largest metro networks, with three lines (Red, Blue, Green) spanning about 69 km; it is complemented by TSRTC city buses and the MMTS suburban rail.
transit.pay: Buy paper QR/token tickets at metro counters or use the T-Savaari app and rechargeable smart cards; city buses take cash or the same smart card. UPI/QR payment is widely accepted.

bus: Intercity buses from MGBS (Imlibun) and JBS (Jubilee) bus stations
train: Secunderabad, Nampally (Hyderabad Deccan), and Kacheguda railway junctions

transit.m: Pushpak AC Airport Liner bus (TSRTC) to Secunderabad, HITEC City, and other hubs (~60-90 min)
Uber/Ola cab to city center (~45-60 min); a metro Airport Express line to Raidurg is under construction

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% at restaurants and ₹20-50 for hotel porters or valet service is appreciated.

food.name: Hyderabadi dum biryani
food.desc: Marinated goat and basmati sealed in a pot and steamed together over low heat, served with mirchi ka salan and onion raita.

places.name: Hotel Shadab
places.note: Old-city classic within walking distance of Charminar, the full Hyderabad atmosphere.

places.name: Shah Ghouse Cafe
places.note: Local favourite for traditional dum-style biryani without the old-city crush.

places.name: Bawarchi
places.note: The original branch, famous for the sign insisting it has no branches.

food.name: Haleem
food.desc: Wheat, lentils and mutton pounded for hours into a silky paste, finished with fried onion, mint and lime; a Ramzan season obsession.

places.name: Pista House
places.note: The most awarded haleem maker in the city and the one that exports it worldwide.

places.name: Shah Ghouse Cafe
places.note: Queues around the block for its haleem through the fasting month.

places.name: Cafe Bahar
places.note: Running since 1973; milder seasoning that suits first-timers.

food.name: Nihari and paya
food.desc: Trotters and shank simmered overnight into a gelatinous, marrow-heavy gravy, eaten at dawn with khameeri roti in the old city.

places.name: Hotel Nayaab
places.note: Breakfast institution for nihari, paya and kheema, open from very early.

places.name: Hotel Shadab
places.note: Serves nihari and khichdi-kheema alongside the biryani, all morning.

places.name: Pista House
places.note: Reliable old-city kitchen if you want the dish outside dawn hours.

food.name: Bagara baingan and mirchi ka salan
food.desc: Baby aubergines in a tamarind, peanut and sesame gravy, and its chilli cousin; the Hyderabadi curries that always shadow the biryani.

places.name: Hotel Shadab
places.note: Both curries done in the old-city style and ordered alongside the rice.

places.name: Shah Ghouse Cafe
places.note: Generous salan portions that come free with most biryani orders.

places.name: Cafe Bahar
places.note: Easy sit-down spot to try the vegetarian side of Hyderabadi cooking.

food.name: Osmania biscuits and bun maska
food.desc: Soft, faintly salty-sweet butter biscuits made for dunking in chai, plus a split bun slathered with butter at the Irani cafes.

places.name: Subhan Bakery
places.note: The bakery Hyderabadis buy Osmania biscuits from by the kilo box.

places.name: Nimrah Cafe and Bakery
places.note: Biscuits still warm, eaten on the steps facing the Charminar.

places.name: Karachi Bakery
places.note: Heritage bakery best known for fruit biscuits, with Osmania alongside.

food.name: Double ka meetha
food.desc: Fried bread soaked in cardamom-saffron milk and sugar syrup, topped with nuts; the Nizami wedding dessert that follows every biryani.

places.name: Hotel Shadab
places.note: Dessert counter also does qubani ka meetha with cream.

places.name: Shah Ghouse Cafe
places.note: Rich version served warm, a standard end to the meal here.

places.name: Cafe Bahar
places.note: Keeps both double ka meetha and qubani ka meetha on the menu daily.

food.name: Irani chai
food.desc: Milk simmered for hours with tea decoction, poured strong and sweet into a thick glass cup; the currency of old-city conversation.

places.name: Nimrah Cafe and Bakery
places.note: The most famous chai counter in the city, right beside the monument.

places.name: Cafe Niloufer
places.note: Creamy Irani chai and bun maska, busy from before sunrise to late night.

places.name: Hotel Subhan
places.note: No-frills chai stop where rickshaw drivers and office workers stand side by side.

food.name: Sharbat-e-mohabbat
food.desc: Rose-scented cold milk poured over crushed watermelon and ice, sold outside the old city mosques and unbeatable in the Deccan heat.

places.name: Charminar street stalls
places.note: Carts appear around the monument and Mecca Masjid, at their peak in Ramzan.

places.name: Moazzam Jahi Market
places.note: Historic market known for fruit, ice cream and cold milk drinks.

places.name: Pista House
places.note: Sells sharbat and falooda beside the haleem counter in season.

landmarks: Charminar
This 16th-century mosque and monument with four grand arches and minarets is the beating heart of Hyderabad's Old City and its most photographed symbol.
Golconda Fort
A massive hilltop fortress of the Qutb Shahi dynasty famous for its ingenious acoustics and sweeping sunset views over the city.
Qutb Shahi Tombs
An atmospheric necropolis of domed granite mausoleums near Golconda that offers some of the city's most evocative Indo-Persian architecture.
Hussain Sagar Lake
A vast man-made lake with a towering monolithic Buddha statue rising from its center, best photographed at sunset from the Tank Bund.
Chowmahalla Palace
The opulent former seat of the Nizams, with grand courtyards, chandeliers, and a stunning Durbar Hall that epitomizes Hyderabadi royal splendor.
Falaknuma Palace
A scorpion-shaped 19th-century palace turned luxury hotel, perched on a hill with breathtaking views and lavish European interiors.
Mecca Masjid
One of India's oldest and largest mosques, built with bricks said to contain soil from Mecca, standing steps from the Charminar.
Birla Mandir
A gleaming white marble hilltop Hindu temple whose intricate carvings and panoramic city views make it a favorite photo spot at dusk.
Salar Jung Museum
One of the world's largest one-man art collections, housed in a grand building famous for its rare musical clock and eclectic global artifacts.
Spanish Mosque (Iqbal-ud-Dowla Mosque)
A unique Moorish-Gothic mosque inside the Paigah Palace grounds, prized by photographers for its unusual Spanish-style architecture rare in India.

train.note: No international trains. Secunderabad Junction is the principal station, with Hyderabad Deccan (Nampally) and Kacheguda also taking long-distance services - they are several kilometres apart, so check your ticket. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead; the overnight trains to Bengaluru, Chennai and Mumbai are the useful ones.

bus.note: No international coaches. The Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station (Imlibun) is the main terminal, with TSRTC (https://www.tsrtconline.in/) running across Telangana and beyond; private Volvo sleepers to Bengaluru, Chennai, Goa and Mumbai leave from Miyapur, LB Nagar and Ameerpet and are bookable on redBus (https://www.redbus.in/).

ferry.note: Hyderabad is landlocked on the Deccan plateau, so there are no ferries. Small pleasure launches cross Hussain Sagar lake to the Buddha statue in the city centre, but these are sightseeing rides rather than transport.

half.name: Ramoji Film City
half.blurb: A vast working film studio complex about 30 kilometers from the city, with themed sets, gardens, and stunt shows open to visitors.

half.name: Ananthagiri Hills
half.blurb: A hill station near Vikarabad with coffee plantations, waterfalls, and the Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple, about two hours from Hyderabad.

full.name: Warangal
full.blurb: A former Kakatiya dynasty capital about 150 kilometers away, with a ruined fort, the carved Thousand Pillar Temple, and Pakhal Lake.

full.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam & Nagarjunakonda
full.blurb: One of the world's largest masonry dams on the Krishna River, with a boat ride to an island of ancient Buddhist ruins, about three hours from Hyderabad.
